model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the mean effect sizes for six different language model variants—mBERT-L₂, XLM-L₂, mBERT-R₂, XLM-R₂, mBERT-B₂, and XLM-B₂—across nine linguistic categories: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic family, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic. The horizontal axis lists these linguistic categories in order from left to right, while the vertical axis represents the effect size, scaled linearly from 0 to 30, with tick marks at intervals of 10. Each linguistic category has six grouped bars, each corresponding to one of the six model variants, distinguished by color: light blue for mBERT-L₂, dark blue for XLM-L₂, light green for mBERT-R₂, dark green for XLM-R₂, light pink for mBERT-B₂, and dark red for XLM-B₂. Error bars extend vertically from each bar, indicating the standard deviation or uncertainty in the mean effect. The bars are not sorted; they appear in the order of the linguistic categories along the x-axis. Visually, the tallest bars are in the IE-Indic category (with mBERT-R₂ reaching approximately 20 and XLM-B₂ around 22), followed by the Semitic category (with XLM-B₂ at approximately 20). The shortest bars are generally in the Isolate category, where all model variants show effect sizes below 2, with some near zero. The chart does not highlight any specific bars with shading, bolding, or annotations beyond the standard color-coding and error bars.
